method.note: Live authorities remain canonical. This artifact is a compact research snapshot. US, Canada, Australia and ECB FX are required preflight inputs. NZ and Japan are not required_for_trader_preflight; a blocked RBNZ source or a Japan holiday-calendar print stays visible on that source and does not by itself mark the packet stale. NZ-dependent and JP-dependent expressions still fail closed. The official RBNZ B2 XLSX is tried first, including a browser-TLS retry, then the official RBNZ B2 HTML table. No vendor or media substitute is used. Japan JGB freshness uses the Tokyo business-day calendar and a one-session publication lag. Euro-area Bund (Germany) and Japan JGB cash curves remain six-economy rate legs. Cross-country spreads use exact common observation dates only. Policy-path context uses official overnight benchmarks plus public money-market data. The required tradable paper rates universe remains SOFR via CME SR3, CORRA via MX CRA, and AONIA via ASX IB. TONA is included when JPX OSE 3M settlements pass identity checks; FST3/€STR stays observe_only until a public settlement feed is reliable. Official government zero/forward curves are supplemental bond-curve inputs and are not required to manufacture a swap curve. Euro-area sovereign fragmentation (IT/FR/ES vs Bund) is market context, never an EA temperature input. Housing context is collected for the US, Canada and Australia from free maintained public sources: FHFA/Census/Fed/Freddie Mac via FRED for the US, Statistics Canada/CMHC/Bank of Canada for Canada, and ABS/RBA for Australia. EA/JP housing is omitted until an official/free source meets the contract. CFTC TFF supplies trader-class ownership/crowding context and can mark the packet stale. CME's public volume/open-interest service is a supplemental overlay and does not flip packet status. No historical warehouse is written to GitHub or Supabase.

sources.snippet: European Central Bank Governing Council member Olli Rehn said the Middle East energy shock hasn’t so far spread to other prices or wages, but those impacts can’t be ruled out.

sources.headline: Lescure Says France Is Far From Needing ECB Help on Debt
sources.snippet: French Finance Minister Roland Lescure said the country is far from needing the European Central Bank to step in even as it wrestles with soaring bond yields.

sources.headline: Google, Constellation Near Billion-Dollar Deal for Nuclear Power
sources.snippet: Google parent Alphabet Inc. is close to an agreement to buy nuclear energy from Constellation Energy Corp., as technology companies race to line up power for the data-center boom.

sources.headline: Global Oil Supply Buffer Running ‘Scarily Thin,’ Aramco CEO Says
sources.snippet: The oil stockpiles that cushion the world from supply shocks have become “scarily thin,” putting markets at risk of worsening unless the Strait of Hormuz reopens, according to the head of Saudi Arabia’s Aramco.

sources.headline: Iran’s Oil Minister Resigns as Exports Dry Up Under US Pressure
sources.snippet: Iran’s Oil Minister Mohsen Paknejad resigned citing personal reasons, as the Islamic Republic tries to sustain its oil industry under a tightening US blockade.

sources.headline: LNG Trade Through Hormuz Extends Rebound Despite Shipping Risks
sources.snippet: Shipments of liquefied natural gas through the Strait of Hormuz extended a rebound that began in September, as the region’s producers seek to restore supplies to energy-starved customers.

sources.headline: Euro-Zone Inflation Tops Estimates to Hit Three-Year High
sources.snippet: Euro-area inflation quickened more than expected to the highest in three years, bolstering expectations that the European Central Bank will lift interest rates further.

sources.headline: UK Firms Predict Faster Price Increases After Energy Costs Surge
sources.snippet: The resurgence in oil and gas prices drove up UK businesses’ inflation expectations as firms planned to pass on cost increases to consumers.

sources.headline: Pimco’s Stracke Says AI Spending Drove Yields, Not Inflation
sources.snippet: Surging capital demand from hyperscalers and the AI ecosystem—not inflation expectations—is the primary force pushing real rates and bond yields higher, Pimco’s Stracke said.

sources.headline: China Oil Comeback Loses Steam as Iran War Drags On
sources.snippet: A nascent recovery in Chinese oil demand has begun to falter, as continued fighting in the Middle East and limited Iranian supply keep crude prices too high for private refiners.

sources.headline: Man Group Says 5.5% Yields Risk Cracking AI Capex, US Consumer
sources.snippet: Man Group’s Kristina Hooper warned that surging long-end Treasury yields threaten AI capital expenditures and US consumer resilience.
